close_reason: Implemented build_ocsp_request producing OcspRequestBytes{body, content_type=application/ocsp-request}. SHA-1 and SHA-256 supported via OcspHashAlg enum (non-exhaustive). CertID built with x509-ocsp's Request::from_cert::<D>. Test oracle is openssl ocsp -no_nonce -reqout, byte-for-byte equal for both algorithms. Additional regression test confirms (cert, issuer) argument order matters. No nonce in v0.x (acceptance criterion explicitly defers). Committed at f1a03899.
description:
## Why

To POST an OCSP query to a responder, pkix-revocation-http must build a DER-encoded OCSPRequest (RFC 6960 §4.1.1). The cert + issuer are inputs; the request body and content-type are outputs the fetcher can POST.

The `x509-ocsp` 0.2 crate (already a dep of pkix-revocation when ocsp feature is on) provides `x509_ocsp::OcspRequest` and `OcspRequestBuilder`. We build on top.

## What

Public helper:

```rust
pub struct OcspRequestBytes {
    pub body: Vec<u8>,           // DER-encoded OCSPRequest
    pub content_type: &'static str, // "application/ocsp-request"
}

pub fn build_ocsp_request(
    cert: &Certificate,
    issuer: &Certificate,
    hash_alg: OcspHashAlg,
) -> Result<OcspRequestBytes, BuildError>;
```

Where:
- `OcspHashAlg` is an enum: `Sha1`, `Sha256` (RFC 6960 mandates SHA-1 support; SHA-256 widely deployed).
- The helper builds CertID (RFC 6960 §4.1.1) with:
  - `hashAlgorithm` — AlgorithmIdentifier wrapping the chosen hash OID.
  - `issuerNameHash` — hash of the issuer's distinguishedName (DER of issuer.tbs_certificate.subject).
  - `issuerKeyHash` — hash of the issuer's subject public key BIT STRING value (no algorithm prefix; just the public key bits per RFC 6960 §4.1.1).
  - `serialNumber` — cert.tbs_certificate.serial_number.

Single CertID per request (multiple CertIDs in one request is RFC-allowed but rarely implemented; out of scope for v0.x).

Optional nonce extension is a separate concern — defer to a follow-up bead. For v0.x, no nonce.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Helper produces DER bytes that round-trip through x509-ocsp::OcspRequest::from_der().
- [ ] Both SHA-1 and SHA-256 supported and tested.
- [ ] CertID fields are byte-for-byte equal to what `openssl ocsp -reqout` produces against the same cert pair (independent oracle).
- [ ] Test fixtures: 2-3 cert+issuer pairs with hand-computed expected request DER (or computed once via openssl + committed as hex literals).
- [ ] No nonce in v0.x; documented as known limitation.

## Out of scope

- Nonce extension (RFC 6960 §4.4.1).
- Multiple-CertID requests.
- Signed OCSP requests (RFC 6960 §4.1.2.2 — almost never used).

## Effort

~150 lines + tests + 2-3 fixture pairs.
